articles.title: Aaron Rodgers’ growing confidence has Steelers believing a deep playoff run is within reach
articles.standfirst: The timing, communication, and chemistry with key targets have become a major asset
articles.summary: The timing, communication, and chemistry with key targets have become a major asset
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers entered last season hoping that Aaron Rodgers could elevate the franchise back into championship contention. One year later, the organization appears even more convinced that goal is attainable.

From the opening days of training camp in Latrobe, Rodgers has looked comfortable, confident, and fully in command of the offense. More importantly, the veteran quarterback appears to be operating on the same wavelength as the pass-catchers around him, a development that has generated optimism throughout the organization as Pittsburgh prepares for the 2026 season.

While every training camp brings its share of encouraging reports, there is a noticeable difference in the way the Steelers are talking about Rodgers this summer. The timing, communication, and chemistry that occasionally took time to develop during his first season in Pittsburgh now appear far more natural. That has been evident in virtually every practice session.

Rodgers has a deep understanding with key targets

Rodgers has continued to work effectively with veteran targets such as DK Metcalf, tight ends Pat Freiermuth and Darnell Washington , and wide receiver Roman Wilson . The familiarity built over the past year has allowed the offense to operate with a greater level of precision, whether the play calls involve quick underneath routes, intermediate throws over the middle, or the deep shots that have long been a hallmark of Rodgers' game.

The progress is particularly important because Rodgers has always been known as a quarterback who demands precision from his receivers. Throughout his NFL career, he has placed a premium on route discipline, pre-snap recognition, and constant communication. Receivers who understand exactly what Rodgers is seeing tend to earn his trust quickly. Those who don't often find themselves learning difficult lessons.

Last season included moments of adjustment as Rodgers and his new teammates learned each other's tendencies. This summer, however, the offense has looked far more synchronized. Michael Pittman Jr. and Germie Bernard are still expected to play meaningful roles within the offense, but the returning connections Rodgers has developed with several of his key targets have been among the most encouraging storylines of camp.

One player drawing particular praise is Roman Wilson

The young receiver has consistently flashed throughout camp and appears to be benefiting from another offseason working alongside the future Hall of Fame quarterback. Steelers assistant general manager Andy Weidl recently highlighted Wilson's development and the growing relationship between him and Rodgers.

Those comments reflect what many observers have noticed throughout camp. Wilson appears more decisive, more comfortable, and more capable of taking advantage of opportunities within the offense. Having Rodgers' trust can significantly accelerate a receiver's growth, and Wilson seems to be reaping the benefits.

The significance extends beyond any one player for the Steelers. The organization believes it has assembled one of the most complete offensive groups Rodgers has worked with in recent years. Metcalf remains one of the league's premier physical receivers. Freiermuth continues to provide reliability in the middle of the field.

Washington offers a unique size mismatch at tight end. Pittman adds another proven weapon, while younger players such as Wilson continue to develop. Combined with Rodgers' experience and football intelligence, the result is an offense that could be considerably more dangerous than the version opponents faced a year ago.

articles.title: Mike McCarthy faces another ordeal at Steelers press conference caused by reporter's cell phone
articles.standfirst: The new Pittsburgh coach found plenty to fix after young quarterbacks struggled against New York
articles.summary: The new Pittsburgh coach found plenty to fix after young quarterbacks struggled against New York
articles.body:
M ike McCarthy ’s frustration was already visible before a ringing phone cut through his postgame press conference.

After watching the Pittsburgh Steelers struggle through a lifeless offensive performance against the New York Jets , the new head coach had little interest in dealing with any additional distractions.

The Steelers were shut out 17-0 at Acrisure Stadium on Friday night, leaving McCarthy with plenty of concerns to address. While explaining where his offense fell short, a reporter’s cell phone interrupted the room, prompting an immediate response from the veteran coach.

“Please, shut that thing off. I mean, my goodness,” McCarthy said.

McCarthy quickly moved on, but the moment captured the mood around Pittsburgh after a night where the offense failed to build on the promise shown in the team’s opening preseason game.

The Steelers had previously impressed in a 28-9 win over the Green Bay Packers , but the performance against New York was a significant step backward.

With Aaron Rodgers and Mason Rudolph rested, Pittsburgh turned to young quarterbacks Will Howard and Drew Allar , but neither was able to consistently challenge the Jets defense.

Howard started the game and completed 10 of 15 passes for 74 yards, but two interceptions in the first half ended promising drives. Allar entered later and finished 11 of 23 for 110 yards while being sacked three times.

“There will definitely be more to clean up this week than last week,” McCarthy said. “That’s the reality of tonight.”

The Steelers ’ offense struggled across the board, finishing with only 98 rushing yards on 26 attempts.

Running back Kaleb Johnson received an extended opportunity, recording 39 yards on 10 carries, but Pittsburgh was unable to establish enough balance to support its young quarterbacks.

McCarthy pointed to missed opportunities in the passing game, including a lack of separation from receivers and an inability to win contested catches.

“We failed to make contested catches,” McCarthy said.

The new Steelers coach believes the difficult outing can still provide value as the team prepares for the regular season.

“We will have great ‘teaching film,’” McCarthy added. “We’re a staff that loves to teach.”

Learning experience for Pittsburgh’s young quarterbacks

The loss provided a reminder that preseason development rarely follows a straight line.

Howard and Allar both showed flashes in previous appearances, but the Jets exposed areas where Pittsburgh’s young quarterbacks still need refinement. Howard acknowledged that the key now is avoiding repeated mistakes.

“The biggest thing is getting to the film and not letting these mistakes fester and not letting one or two mistakes turn into more,” Howard said.

With Rodgers expected to take control of the offense once the regular season begins, the preseason remains focused on evaluating depth and identifying which young players can contribute.

McCarthy ’s staff now has plenty of film to analyze before the Steelers ’ final preseason matchup against the Buffalo Bills .

McCarthy ’s reaction to the phone interruption may have been the most memorable moment of the night, but the real issue facing Pittsburgh is much bigger.

The offense must find consistency before the games start counting. After an impressive opening performance and a frustrating follow-up, McCarthy knows exactly what his team needs next, and that is improvement.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers has company: Steelers close to finalizing quarterback room for 2026
articles.standfirst: Head coach Mike McCarthy could make a stunning decision in his first season with the Pittsburgh Steelers.
articles.summary: Head coach Mike McCarthy could make a stunning decision in his first season with the Pittsburgh Steelers.
articles.body:
This past offseason was one filled with a major shakeup for the Pittsburgh Steelers . Longtime head coach Mike Tomlin departed the team, which in turn put Aaron Rodgers ' future with the franchise in doubt as well.

In came Rodgers' former head coach, Mike McCarthy , to try to sway him into coming back. While that ultimately worked, it took until mid-May for Rodgers to make his final decision to return for one more season. By that point, though, the Steelers had covered their bases at the quarterback position.

With Will Howard on the roster heading into his sophomore season and Mason Rudolph returning for the final year of his contract, the Steelers drafted Penn State quarterback Drew Allar in the third round of the 2026 NFL Draft . Once Rodgers confirmed his return, that left the team with four quarterbacks with starting potential on the roster.

Will Howard and Drew Allar both slated to make Steelers 53-man roster

It's very uncommon for an NFL team to play out a season with four quarterbacks on the 53-man roster . While the Steelers haven't decided just yet what they're going to do once the regular season begins, Gerry Dulac of the Pittsburgh Post-Gazette reported on Saturday that t he team is committed to rolling with both Howard and Allar on the roster going forward .

Logically, that would leave Rudolph as the odd man out . The problem is that neither Howard or Allar have any NFL experience. Going into a season with a 42-year-old Rodgers being backed up by two inexperienced quarterbacks could prove risky.

But if Allar and Howard are both going to be on the roster this season, Rudolph could very well be traded before Week 1 to a team in need of a veteran backup.

articles.title: Bills-Steelers: Where to watch the Week 4 preseason game and what time does it start?
articles.standfirst: Buffalo hosts Pittsburgh on Thursday night in the final preseason game for both teams.
articles.summary: Buffalo hosts Pittsburgh on Thursday night in the final preseason game for both teams.
articles.body:
The Buffalo Bills and Pittsburgh Steelers bring their 2026 preseason schedules to a close on Thursday night when they meet at Highmark Stadium in Orchard Park, New York.

Buffalo enters the matchup with a perfect 2-0 preseason record after beating the Carolina Panthers 29-14 and following that with an emphatic 31-7 victory over the Cleveland Browns .

Pittsburgh is 1-1 after two games. The Steelers opened with a 28-9 victory against the Green Bay Packers before suffering a 17-0 defeat to the New York Jets .

The final exhibition gives both coaching staffs another opportunity to evaluate players fighting for roster spots before attention turns fully toward the regular season.

What time does Bills vs Steelers start?

Bills vs Steelers takes place on Thursday, August 27, with kickoff scheduled for 7:00 p.m. ET at Highmark Stadium.

For viewers elsewhere in the United States, that means a 6:00 p.m. CT, 5:00 p.m. MT and 4:00 p.m. PT start.

The matchup is the third and final preseason game for both Buffalo and Pittsburgh.

Buffalo begins its regular season on September 13 against the Houston Texans , while Pittsburgh opens its campaign on the same day at home against the Atlanta Falcons .

Where to watch Bills vs Steelers

Fans in the Buffalo market can watch the game locally on WIVB, while NFL Network will also carry the matchup for viewers outside the local markets, subject to NFL broadcast restrictions.

In Pittsburgh, the game will be shown on KDKA-TV CBS and through the Steelers ' preseason television affiliate network.

Fans located within eligible Steelers markets can also stream the game through Steelers.com or the official Steelers mobile app. Geographic restrictions apply.

NFL+ Premium provides another option in the United States for watching live out-of-market preseason games on supported devices.

International viewers can access the game through NFL Game Pass on DAZN in eligible countries. Steelers fans in Ireland can also stream the matchup through Steelers.com and the team's official app.

Radio coverage is available through each team's respective networks, including 97 Rock for Buffalo and WDVE 102.5 FM and WBGG 970 AM for Pittsburgh.

articles.title: Mike McCarthy's latest Steelers decision could affect the future of Aaron Rodgers
articles.standfirst: Pittsburgh kept Mason Rudolph, Will Howard and Drew Allar, giving McCarthy an unusually crowded quarterback room
articles.summary: Pittsburgh kept Mason Rudolph, Will Howard and Drew Allar, giving McCarthy an unusually crowded quarterback room
articles.body:
The Pittsburgh Steelers are entering the 2026 NFL season with an unusually crowded quarterback room, and Mike McCarthy appears perfectly comfortable with it.

Pittsburgh finalized its 53-man roster by keeping Mason Rudolph, Will Howard and Drew Allar behind starter Aaron Rodgers , confirming what McCarthy had strongly hinted at after the preseason finale against Buffalo .

Asked whether all four quarterbacks had earned spots, McCarthy called that “a very accurate evaluation.”

“I feel good about the quarterback room,” McCarthy added. “I've been saying it for quite some time, and they've showed it on the field. We got two veterans that we can win with, and we got two young guys that we're excited about the future.”

The decision is notable because McCarthy has never previously carried four quarterbacks into Week 1 during his head-coaching career. It also reflects two competing priorities.

Pittsburgh needs a reliable veteran behind the 42-year-old Rodgers , which makes Rudolph an obvious insurance policy, but the Steelers also want enough time to develop both Howard and Allar without sacrificing either one.

Rudolph gives Steelers stability

Rudolph ’s preseason workload was limited, but his standing improved as Howard and Allar endured uneven performances over the final two games.

Howard threw multiple interceptions during the preseason, including one against Buffalo that immediately left him visibly frustrated. Allar, meanwhile, showed flashes but also struggled with consistency and pressure in his first NFL action.

Rudolph believes his experience and familiarity with the offense make him a natural fit behind Rodgers .

“I think I can execute all the same concepts,” Rudolph said. “I like a lot of the same concepts... I think I've had a good camp, and I like the way that the offense is evolving and trending.”

With Rodgers in the final stages of his career, Pittsburgh couldn't realistically enter the season with only developmental options behind him. That doesn't mean the Steelers are giving up on Howard or Allar .

Time to develop both young quarterbacks

Allar said the preseason gave him valuable experience even when the results were not perfect.

“I feel good about everything that I put on tape,” Allar said. “I think the biggest thing is, I have a lot of great mentors between players and coaches to learn from, from the things I've done well and also the mistakes I've had.”

McCarthy has repeatedly argued that carrying four quarterbacks can help rather than hinder development.

“I'd have six quarterbacks in a building if it worked,” he said. “I think that would be very healthy for the overall quarterback room with four quarterbacks.”

The Steelers also activated cornerback Joey Porter Jr. from the physically unable to perform list, avoiding a four-game absence, while safety DeShon Elliott was placed on injured reserve with a designation to return.

Still, the quarterback decision stands out most. Rodgers is the present. Rudolph is the safety net. Howard and Allar represent two different bets on what might come next.

Pittsburgh has chosen not to make that decision yet, and for the first time under McCarthy , all four will begin the season together.

articles.standfirst: Mike Tomlin reveals why Aaron Rodgers gives the Steelers a real Super Bowl chance.
articles.summary: Mike Tomlin reveals why Aaron Rodgers gives the Steelers a real Super Bowl chance.
articles.body:
M ike Tomlin is no longer the head coach of the Pittsburgh Steelers , but he remains fully confident in the organization he led for nearly two decades and believes the team has the necessary pieces to compete for a championship.

During an appearance on The Rich Eisen Show , Tomlin was asked about the Steelers’ chances of reaching the Super Bowl in Mike McCarthy ’s first season as head coach. The former Steelers coach made it clear that he still believes in Pittsburgh’s project and in the impact of Aaron Rodgers as the team’s leader.

“I certainly do,” Tomlin said. “That's the only reason Aaron (Rodgers) comes back. He believes it; I believe it. I don’t think he comes back if he doesn't believe that. They got the bones of having a good unit in all three phases.”

Tomlin also pointed out that the lack of national attention surrounding the Steelers could work in their favor, serving as extra motivation for a team with high expectations.

“Certainly, they are not being talked about compared to how others are being talked about, but that can be a good motivator as well. I think they have high expectations, and I think they should have high expectations.”

The arrival of Aaron Rodgers for another season has raised expectations in Pittsburgh, especially after the Steelers reunited him with Mike McCarthy, the coach who helped him win Super Bowl XLV during their time together with the Green Bay Packers . Now, the two will try to recreate that success in a new chapter with the Steelers.

Tomlin knows this roster better than almost anyone from the outside. He coached many of the Steelers’ current players and was around Rodgers during his first season in Pittsburgh. Now in a different role, he will have the opportunity to evaluate the team from a new perspective.

After stepping down as head coach, Tomlin joined NBC’s Football Night in America as a studio analyst, meaning his opinions on the Steelers will remain part of the conversation throughout the season.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers reveals his definitive retirement plans from the NFL
articles.standfirst: The Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback says the 2026 season will be the end of his playing career, with family life becoming his priority afterward
articles.summary: The Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback says the 2026 season will be the end of his playing career, with family life becoming his priority afterward
articles.body:
A aron Rodgers appears to have finally settled on what comes next after his NFL career, and his plans extend well beyond simply walking away from football.

The Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback has made it clear that the 2026 season is intended to be his final year in the league, bringing an end to a professional career that has already lasted more than two decades.

Rodgers , now 42, previously confirmed in May that he planned to retire after the season, and he has since reiterated that there is no longer any uncertainty surrounding his decision.

Speaking with SiriusXM's Mad Dog Sports Radio, Rodgers offered a glimpse into what he hopes his life will look like once his playing days are over.

Rather than immediately moving toward another football-related role, the veteran quarterback said he is looking forward to spending more time away from the spotlight and building a family with his wife, Brittani .

"I'm looking forward to a life of quiet after 22 years in the pros and three in college," he said.

Rodgers explained that one of his priorities after retirement will be supporting his wife and eventually becoming a father.

He indicated that he hopes to be "supporting my pregnant wife" by this time next year, while subsequently clarifying that he and Brittani are not currently expecting a child.

The distinction is important because Rodgers ' comments were not an announcement of a current pregnancy. Instead, he was describing the future he hopes to have once his football career is finished.

For Rodgers , that future represents a significant change after spending virtually his entire adult life playing football.

He entered the NFL in 2005 after playing three seasons of college football at California and spent the first 18 years of his professional career with the Green Bay Packers .

He won four NFL MVP awards, a Super Bowl and the Super Bowl MVP during his time in Green Bay before moving to the New York Jets in 2023.

His Jets tenure was disrupted by a torn Achilles suffered only four offensive snaps into his first season with the team. After two difficult years in New York, Rodgers moved to Pittsburgh for the 2025 season.

Rodgers sees family life as the next chapter

Rodgers ' decision to continue playing in 2026 was influenced heavily by Pittsburgh's decision to hire Mike McCarthy , his former Green Bay head coach.

The pair worked together for 13 seasons with the Packers , and their reunion ultimately convinced Rodgers to give himself one final NFL campaign.

He signed a one-year contract with Pittsburgh , with the deal providing a clear endpoint to his playing career. NFL Network reported that the agreement included $22 million guaranteed and could be worth as much as $25 million with incentives.

That final season will therefore be about more than simply extending Rodgers ' career. It represents the closing chapter of a 22-year NFL journey.

Rodgers ' comments about fatherhood suggest that he is already thinking seriously about what comes afterward.

He has spoken about enjoying his role as "Uncle Aaron" to his brother's children, and spending time with them has apparently strengthened both his and Brittani's desire to have children themselves.

That personal goal also helps explain why retirement appears increasingly attractive to Rodgers .

Football has dominated his life since his college days, but the quarterback has previously spoken about wanting greater privacy once his career ends.

Brittani has also largely stayed away from the spotlight, with Rodgers explaining that she does not want to become a public figure simply because she married an NFL superstar.

Their relationship itself has remained relatively private. Rodgers confirmed that he secretly married Brittani in 2025, but has shared few details about their marriage publicly.

Now, however, he has offered a clearer indication of what he wants from their life together.

Rodgers ' retirement plans are also notable because there had been genuine uncertainty about whether he would return for another season.

After the Steelers won the AFC North in 2025, there was speculation that Pittsburgh wanted him back, while Rodgers himself took time before deciding whether he still wanted to play. The eventual hiring of McCarthy played a major role in changing his mind.

Once he made the decision, though, Rodgers became increasingly definitive about the ending.

In July, when asked whether he might reconsider his retirement decision, he answered simply: "Zero debate." That leaves Rodgers with one final season to compete before beginning the quieter life he says he wants.

His legacy in football is already secure, with a Hall of Fame career that includes a Super Bowl victory, four MVP awards and years of elite quarterback play. But Rodgers appears more interested now in what comes after those accomplishments.

The next stage will not necessarily involve another team, another contract or another comeback.

Instead, Rodgers is looking toward life away from football, spending more time with his wife, recovering from the physical demands of his career and hopefully becoming a father.

For a player who has spent 22 years in the professional game, retirement will represent a dramatic change. But based on Rodgers' latest comments, it is a change he is increasingly eager to embrace.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers fills DK Metcalf's brain with wild ideas: What is Agartha and why do Steelers players believe in it?
articles.standfirst: Rodgers' outside-the-box thinking has rubbed off on the Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver.
articles.summary: Rodgers' outside-the-box thinking has rubbed off on the Pittsburgh Steelers wide receiver.
articles.body:
There's no denying that Aaron Rodgers became a very polarizing figure late in his NFL career. Once beloved by even casual fans due to his jaw-dropping arm talent and incredible on-field performances, Rodgers began falling out of favor in his late 30s.

In the eyes of some fans, Rodgers’ personality just rubbed them the wrong way . Some thought he was entitled, others didn’t like how he treated his teammates, and some simply didn't like his way of thinking - which was certainly out of the box when it came to topics off of the gridiron .

Now heading into his final NFL season, Rodgers is taking a more holistic approach. He worked to strengthen his bond with his family during the offseason , has stayed out of the spotlight and said all the right things to the media, and is focused on winning games with his Pittsburgh Steelers teammates.

DK Metcalf believes weird things are happening in Antarctica, and fortifies the Hollow Earth theory

But Rodgers’ outside-the-box thinking hasn't subsided. In fact, it has actually rubbed off on his top wide receiver, DK Metcalf . A recent profile of Metcalf written by Jonathan Jones of The Athletic highlighted a shift in thinking the wideout has had, with help from Rodgers.

In the car he would listen to music, of course, but also audiobooks. Topics ranged from Christianity to body language to self-help to conspiracy theories. “Yeah, I’m a big conspiracy theorist,” Metcalf says with a smile. “Shout out to my quarterback.” Metcalf wants to know what is really going on in Antarctica. That is, what’s really going on in Antarctica. “I think it’s another world,” Metcalf says... “I think there is another civilization inside of Earth.”

Metcalf's conspiracy theory seems to align with the concept of " Agartha ", a legendary kingdom opined to be located within the center of the Earth. It's connected with the idea of " Hollow Earth ".

Obviously, Metcalf isn't the only person to believe in such theories. But without Rodgers opening his mind up to new possibilities, perhaps Metcalf would have never even explored the idea.

articles.title: Broad daylight heist: NFL rookie suffers massive $150K property theft
articles.standfirst: Max Iheanachor’s Pittsburgh home was broken into as the first-round pick adjusted to life in the league
articles.summary: Max Iheanachor’s Pittsburgh home was broken into as the first-round pick adjusted to life in the league
articles.body:
Pittsburgh Steelers rookie Max Iheanachor had plenty to manage as he adjusted to life in the NFL . A daylight burglary at his Pittsburgh residence added a far more unsettling problem.

The offensive tackle’s home in the Mount Washington neighborhood was broken into on August 26, with thieves reportedly escaping with jewelry and designer handbags worth somewhere between $150,000 and $250,000.

The incident happened between approximately 10:30 a.m. and 1:30 p.m. after the property had been left secured. When the occupants returned, they found the garage door open and a window smashed.

Investigators believe a rock was thrown through the window to gain entry before the home was ransacked. Police have continued investigating the burglary, but no arrests have been reported.

Preparing for his first NFL action

The timing made the incident particularly disruptive for Iheanachor, who was still working his way back from an injury during his first training camp.

Pittsburgh selected him with the No.21 overall pick in April after an impressive rise through college football.

Iheanachor began at East Los Angeles College before transferring to Arizona State , where he developed into one of the more highly regarded offensive tackles in the country and earned second-team All-Big 12 recognition in 2025.

His first preseason appearance came against Buffalo on August 27, one day after the burglary.

He entered the regular season listed as Pittsburgh’s No.2 right tackle behind Dylan Cook , leaving him with the challenge of earning playing time while also dealing with the aftermath of the break-in.

The Steelers have viewed Iheanachor as a significant piece of their longer-term offensive line plans, but his opening months in the league have already included an injury setback and now a major security incident.

Another NFL player targeted

Iheanachor ’s case comes amid heightened concern around residential burglaries involving professional athletes.

Patrick Mahomes, Travis Kelce and Joe Burrow are among the NFL stars whose homes have previously been targeted, while similar incidents have affected athletes in other major American sports.

Authorities have tied some of those earlier burglaries to organized crime groups. There has been no public evidence connecting the theft at Iheanachor’s home to those cases.

Professional athletes can present an unusual target because much of their schedule is publicly available. Games, practices and team travel can make it easier to predict when a player may be away.

That risk is something Iheanachor has been forced to confront almost immediately after entering the league. His immediate football priority remains carving out a role with Pittsburgh.

Away from the field, however, police are still trying to determine who entered his home and disappeared with valuables reportedly worth well into six figures.

articles.title: DK Metcalf’s conspiracy theory: He claims there’s another civilization on Earth besides humans
articles.standfirst: DK Metcalf, a Pittsburgh Steelers player, points to a conspiracy theory that is gaining significant traction on social media
articles.summary: DK Metcalf, a Pittsburgh Steelers player, points to a conspiracy theory that is gaining significant traction on social media
articles.body:
DK Metcalf , player for the Pittsburgh Steelers of the NFL , has the theory that "Antarctica is another world" and that "there is another civilization inside the Earth" .

'"Yes, I'm a big fan of conspiracy theories," he admitted.'

The famous "wide receiver" , who is entering his eighth season in the NFL and has been selected to the Pro Bowl twice , posed the question to Jonathan Jones in "The Athletic" as to why the leaders of each country travel to Antarctica for some kind of summit.

"Why is there a secret meeting—well, it’s not secret—but why is there a meeting between all the world leaders of all the countries in Antarctica, specifically?" says DeKaylin Metcalf.

'Jonathan Jones: "There is no unified theory about a secret civilization in Antarctica"'

'Jonathan Jones tried to debunk DK Metcalf's conspiracy theory by assuring that "there is no verifiable evidence that such meetings have taken place".'

'"There is no unified theory about a secret civilization in Antarctica," Jones noted.'

There really is a civilization that inhabits the interior of Antarctica... or something like that

Brent Christner , a Steelers fan and associate professor of microbiology at the University of Florida, stated that there is a civilization living inside Antarctica... or something like that .

Christner explained that "deep beneath kilometers of Antarctic ice, there is water and microbes live in it that have existed for hundreds of thousands of years. However, these microbes are so tiny that not even an animal as small as a crab or a slug could survive by feeding on them."

"Without a doubt, there are distinguished visitors who travel to Antarctica. When they arrived, they received first-class treatment: they were taken by helicopter and shown all the most outstanding places. But no G7 summit or anything of the sort is held there," Christner pointed out.

articles.title: “Before we get married, I gotta go f**k this guy”: Aaron Rodgers reveals ex, Shailene Woodley's, wild request after they got engaged
articles.standfirst: Engagement unraveled far earlier than many people realized
articles.summary: Engagement unraveled far earlier than many people realized
articles.body:
Aaron Rodgers has spent years largely avoiding a detailed public account of what ended his engagement to Shailene Woodley . Now, as he approaches what could be his final NFL season, he has offered one of his most direct versions yet.

Speaking on teammate Cam Heyward ’s Not Just Football podcast, Rodgers said the relationship changed dramatically within days of his proposal in December 2020.

“She said yes,” Rodgers said. “A couple days after that she tells me, ‘Before we get married I gotta go f**k this guy.’”

Rodgers didn't identify the person he was referring to, and Woodley has not publicly responded to that specific allegation. He said the engagement was already effectively over by March 2021.

“I proposed in December, took off the ring by March, and we had a couple of times when we tried to get reunited and nothing ever happened,” Rodgers added.

Who was the one that walked away?

Much of Rodgers ’ frustration appeared to center on how the breakup has been discussed publicly since the couple separated.

He said there was “not even a relationship in ’22 to break off” and claimed Woodley had already made her position clear during their attempts to reconcile.

“She literally told me I don’t want to be with you,” Rodgers said.

That account contrasts with the way Woodley has spoken about the emotional fallout from the relationship.

In a 2024 interview, she described going through a “really awful, traumatic” period and said: “I felt like I lost my soul, my self, my happiness, my joy.”

She also said she came to understand “depression and anxiety” in a much deeper way during that time. Rodgers pushed back against any suggestion that he had simply abandoned her.

“Shai, you left me, you took the ring off,” he said. “Her story is that I ruined her life and gave her crazy depression because I left her… What are we talking about regarding me ruining your life?”

Rodgers wants the past left alone

The four-time MVP also made clear that he has little interest in continuing to revisit previous relationships publicly.

“Move on with your life,” Rodgers said. “Don’t mention me.”

Woodley has previously called that period “the darkest, hardest time of my life,” but she hasn't publicly confirmed Rodgers ’ version of how the engagement ended. Rodgers has since remarried and is focused on a much different future.

He has spoken openly about wanting to start a family with his wife, Brittani , and about stepping away from the spotlight once his football career is over.

Before that happens, he still has one more major chapter to write in Pittsburgh. His comments about Woodley , however, suggest there are parts of his past he was not willing to leave unexplained.

articles.title: “Why sacrifice Jed York?”: Aaron Rodgers calls out ESPN double standard for ignoring Dianna Russini scandal then highlighting 49ers controversy
articles.standfirst: Rodgers questioned why the network promoted one NFL scandal so heavily
articles.summary: Rodgers questioned why the network promoted one NFL scandal so heavily
articles.body:
Aaron Rodgers has reignited his criticism of ESPN, arguing that the network has applied a different standard to the Dianna Russini -Mike Vrabel controversy than it has to other embarrassing stories involving prominent NFL figures.

Appearing on teammate Cam Heyward ’s Not Just Football podcast, Rodgers pointed directly to ESPN’s coverage of San Francisco 49ers owner Jed York as an example of what he sees as an inconsistency.

“I also said you’re a gutless organization because they haven’t said anything,” Rodgers said. “They spend so much time on certain issues but you won’t talk one second on the Dianna Russini situation.”

Rodgers contrasted that with coverage of York, who pleaded no contest to disorderly conduct and possessing criminal tools after an incident in Ohio involving an alleged agreement to pay for sex.

“That literally was the number one topic when you click on ESPN.com,” Rodgers stated. “That was the featured story. So you bring in how many millions of eyes to that situation.”

Russini story raises questions beyond gossip

Rodgers ’ criticism wasn't simply that Russini and Vrabel had received less attention. He argued that the situation carried wider implications because prominent NFL reporters can have voting responsibilities tied to major awards.

“Does that have the same effect as a reporter who’s, you know, has alleged intimate relations with a coach who has a vote for MVP, has a vote for coach of the year?” Rodgers added.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers slams Donald Trump over broken campaign promises
articles.standfirst: Rodgers accuses the Trump administration of failing to deliver meaningful change
articles.summary: Rodgers accuses the Trump administration of failing to deliver meaningful change
articles.body:
Aaron Rodgers has launched a blistering attack on Donald Trum p, declaring that the president’s signature MAGA movement is effectively dead because, in his view, Trump hasn’t delivered on many of the promises that helped him win support.

The Pittsburgh Steelers quarterback made the remarks during a recent appearance on teammate Cam Heyward’s “Not Just Football” podcast.

The discussion about American politics quickly turned into a wide-ranging critique of Trump , Washington and the political establishment.

Rodgers questioned what had actually changed since Trump returned to the White House. He pointed to campaign promises involving government reform, vaccines, foreign conflicts and greater transparency, asking whether voters had really seen the transformation they were promised.

“There's no ‘Make America Great Again’,” said Rodgers .

“Trump gets into office running on all these policies. You know, he's going to go after the swamp and go into Fort Knox and cut the vaccine stuff and not go into foreign wars and end the Ukraine stuff and... what's actually happened?'—transparency in the Epstein files; Absolutely nothing.”

He also pushed back against the assumption that his previous views automatically make him a Trump supporter. Rodgers has frequently attracted controversy over his skepticism toward vaccines and mainstream public-health policies, but he insisted that he doesn’t trust politicians from either side of the political divide.

Rodgers turns his criticism toward Washington

Rodgers ’ frustrations weren’t limited to Trump. The veteran quarterback described American politics as a broader failure, arguing that voters have repeatedly been promised major change only to discover that little ultimately improves.

He pointed to previous Democratic administrations under Barack Obama and Joe Biden , questioning whether either had produced the meaningful progress supporters had hoped for. Rodgers also questioned the impact of the Affordable Care Act and whether healthcare in America is substantially better as a result.

Rodgers also criticized what he characterized as a political “uni-party,” suggesting that powerful interests have too much influence over lawmakers. During the conversation, he questioned the role of lobbying organizations in Washington and argued that political labels often obscure how the system actually operates.

The Steelers quarterback went further by taking aim at FBI Director Kash Patel , whom he reportedly called a “moron,” while once again distancing himself from the “Trumper” label.

Rodgers ’ comments are especially notable because of his previous association with figures in Trump’s political orbit. He has maintained a highly publicized relationship with Robert F. Kennedy Jr., largely because of their shared skepticism surrounding vaccines and conventional public-health policies.

Despite his criticism of Trump, Rodgers continues to support Kennedy , who serves as Trump’s secretary of Health and Human Services.

The White House hadn’t publicly responded to Rodgers ’ comments at the time of reporting. This is just the latest chapter in the quarterback’s increasingly outspoken political profile.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers joins Tom Brady in an exclusive NFL club as he prepares for his final season
articles.standfirst: This is the second consecutive season that Aaron Rodgers has been the oldest player in the NFL
articles.summary: This is the second consecutive season that Aaron Rodgers has been the oldest player in the NFL
articles.body:
Aaron Rodgers returns to the Pittsburgh Steelers for his 22nd and final season of a legendary, Hall of Fame career. Rodgers will be playing again with Mike McCarthy , with whom he previously spent 13 seasons together in Green Bay , winning a Super Bowl and securing two of Rodgers' four MVP awards.

Last season, Rodgers led Pittsburgh to the postseason, clinching the AFC North with a 10-6 record, a 65.7% completion rate, 24 touchdowns, and seven interceptions . Now, a new era for the Pittsburgh Steelers begins without Mike Tomlin , who, in his 19 seasons as head coach, never suffered a single losing season.

They will open the campaign at home against the Atlanta Falcons with Cooper Rush at quarterback , followed by an away game against the New England Patriots, and then a home game against the Cincinnati Bengals .

Aaron Rodgers Matches Tom Brady's Longevity Milestone

As he embarks on his farewell campaign, Rodgers joins Tom Brady as the only quarterbacks since 1950 to start Week 1 at age 42 or older . Brady ultimately played until he was 45, capturing a ring at age 43 with the Tampa Bay Buccaneers in 2020.

Throughout this upcoming schedule, Rodgers also has one final opportunity to join an exclusive, historic circle consisting of Tom Brady , Peyton Manning , Drew Brees , and Brett Favre , the only signal-callers who have successfully defeated all 32 current NFL franchises.

While legendary names like Joe Montana and Fran Tarkenton belong in the conversation, they lacked the chance to face every modern team, though they did notch at least one victory against every franchise active during their respective eras.

Turning 43 years old during the 2026 season , Rodgers has not surpassed 4,000 passing yards or 30 touchdowns in a single year since 2021 .

The external pressure to deliver immediately will be intense; the Steelers have not won a playoff game since 2016 and currently carry a franchise-record streak of seven consecutive postseason losses .

With a restructured roster, a reunion with his former Green Bay play-caller, and a ticking clock on his professional journey, the stage is set for a dramatic final chapter in the Steel City.

articles.standfirst: Steelers and Falcons open the 2026 season at Acrisure Stadium with Pittsburgh as the favorite
articles.summary: Steelers and Falcons open the 2026 season at Acrisure Stadium with Pittsburgh as the favorite
articles.body:
The NFL season is underway, and Week 1 kicks off with an interconference matchup: the Pittsburgh Steelers host the Atlanta Falcons at Acrisure Stadium. It's a clash between the old school of the AFC North and an NFC South franchise looking to make a splash on the road.

With zero games played by all teams, this is literally the starting point of the campaign, and both teams will be out there making their mark from the first Sunday.

Falcons vs Steelers: Schedule and where to watch the Week 1 game

The Steelers' home game is scheduled for Sunday, September 13, 2026. According to the official schedule, the kickoff for this Week 1 game falls within the NFL's classic Sunday afternoon block, which will be:

Since this NFL game is a Sunday afternoon game, the broadcast window corresponds to Sunday afternoon networks. In this case, the Steelers vs. Falcons game will be on FOX and streamed on NFL+ Premium.

The game is being played at Acrisure Stadium in Pittsburgh, which has a capacity of 68,400. It's one of the toughest venues in the league for a visiting team, especially in Week 1, when the Steelers' fans arrive with renewed energy after the preseason break.

Playing at home in this venue gives Pittsburgh a significant environmental advantage against an opponent who will have to adjust to the noise and intensity from the first snap.

What are the odds for Falcons vs Steelers?

The bookmakers have Pittsburgh as the clear favorite at home ; the moneyline places the Steelers at odds of 1.60, with an implied probability of 61.9%, while the Falcons pay 2.66, with a 38.1% implied probability of taking the victory to Atlanta.

The point spread is set at 3.5 points: Pittsburgh is the favorite at -3.5 (odds 2.01) and Atlanta is the underdog at +3.5 (odds 1.91). It's a tight spread—essentially the classic "field goal plus one"—suggesting the market expects a close game despite the favorite's advantage.

As for the combined total points, the main line is around 41.5 to 42.5 points. At 41.5, both the Over and Under pay 1.92, a near-perfect spread that reflects uncertainty about the offensive rhythm of both teams in their first official game of the year.

The market is clear on this and there are reasons to back it up: the home advantage of Acrisure Stadium , the implied probability and a manageable spread all point to a Pittsburgh victory.

However, the narrow margin and even total call for caution: I expect a Steelers victory by a margin of between 3 and 7 points, in a game that comes down to the fourth quarter. If Atlanta protects the ball well, the +3.5 bet has value for hedgers. Our prediction is a Pittsburgh Steelers 24-20 Atlanta Falcons game.

For the Steelers, defending Acrisure Stadium in Week 1 is a priority: starting 1-0 at home sets the tone for the entire season in an AFC North that is historically defined by very close margins. For the Falcons, stealing a road victory against a clear favorite would be the kind of result that redefines expectations from the outset.

The total around 42 points suggests a balanced game, neither an offensive explosion nor a pure trench war. The team that wins the battle on third downs and avoids turnovers will have the decisive advantage; in a game so close in the betting lines, a turnover or a well-executed long drive could tip the scales.

Implications for the 2026-2027 NFL season

Since it's opening week, no team has a win or loss record yet: everyone starts at 0-0. That's precisely why every result in Week 1 carries weight. A Pittsburgh win would immediately put them in the early race for the AFC North title; an Atlanta upset would send a strong message in the NFC South race and give them a valuable psychological cushion for the first few weeks.

articles.summary: Aaron Rodgers’ classy gesture to Mike McCarthy after Steelers’ emotional Week 1 victory.
articles.body:
A aron Rodgers gave Mike McCarthy a dream start as head coach of the Pittsburgh Steelers . After the victory over the Atlanta Falcons , the veteran quarterback made a special gesture by handing the game ball to his new coach, who secured his first win at the helm of the franchise.

“It's always special when it is the first one in a place that is extra special,” Rodgers said after the game.

The Steelers defeated the Falcons 20-13 in a matchup where Rodgers delivered a solid performance in his official debut with Pittsburgh. The veteran quarterback completed 24 of 40 passes for 221 yards and a touchdown, showing flashes of the talent that made him one of the best passers of his generation.

The connection between Rodgers and McCarthy once again became a major storyline. The two previously found success together with the Green Bay Packers, where they won Super Bowl XLV more than a decade ago, and now they are attempting to recreate that winning formula in Pittsburgh.

Although the Steelers’ offense had some struggles, especially in the running game, the defense ultimately made the difference in securing the victory. T.J. Watt delivered the game-changing play by returning an interception for a touchdown (pick-six) in the fourth quarter, sealing McCarthy’s first win as Pittsburgh’s head coach.

The victory represents a positive beginning for McCarthy, who took over after the departure of Mike Tomlin and now faces the challenge of maintaining the winning culture of one of the NFL’s most historic franchises.

articles.title: Aaron Rodgers' singular gesture with Mike McCarthy that surprised after the Steelers' victory What was special about it?
articles.standfirst: After the Steelers' victory over the Falcons, the quarterback handed his coach the game ball.
articles.summary: After the Steelers' victory over the Falcons, the quarterback handed his coach the game ball.
articles.body:
A aron Rodgers was in charge of putting the finishing touch on a special day for Mike McCarth y, since he knew what that victory meant for Mike.

It is McCarthy's first victory since taking office in Pittsburgh . His team's quarterback handed the coach the game ball after the Steelers' 20-13 win over the Falcons

It's the team you supported as a child

Rodgers explained after the game why he considered his coach’s victory special. McCarthy was not only opening his win column with the Steelers . He was doing it with the team he had followed since he was a child.

«Mike has won many times, but it is always special when it is the first time in a place, and even more special when it is with the team you have supported since you were a child», Rodgers said.

The quarterback also recalled that McCarthy 's parents still live in the area. For the coach, returning to Pittsburgh to lead the Steelers represented a direct link to his personal history.

McCarthy received the ball and was grateful for both Rodgers' recognition and that of his players. “First team ball, first win, so obviously a special moment”, said the coach, before insisting that the team now had to focus on the next objective.

A victory built from defense

The result was positive for Pittsburgh, although the offense struggled for much of the game. Rodgers completed 24 of 40 passes for 221 yards and a touchdown in his first official game of the season.

The defense kept the team afloat in the decisive moments. T.J. Watt was the star with two sacks and an interception returned 35 yards for a touchdown in the fourth quarter.

The Steelers thus left with a 1-0 record and McCarthy with his first game ball for a win as the franchise's head coach. Rodgers, one of the players who knows the coach best, was the one in charge of handing it to him.

articles.standfirst: The Steelers are still far from being Super Bowl contenders, but Rodgers had a good start to his last season in the NFL
articles.summary: The Steelers are still far from being Super Bowl contenders, but Rodgers had a good start to his last season in the NFL
articles.body:
The NFL Week 1 schedule is officially in the books, and it delivered something truly unprecedented and historic: for the first time ever , a 16-game week concluded with every single matchup finishing with a completely unique point differential, meaning every team won by a different margin of victory.

It also stands as the highest-scoring kickoff weekend in NFL history with a staggering 791 total points , spearheaded by the Chicago Bears dropping 59 points, while surprisingly, the Los Angeles Rams were the only squad across the entire league failing to crack double digits during the opening slate of the 2026 season.

Aaron Rodgers Calls Out Officials After Steelers Opener

Among the most captivating matchups of the weekend was the Pittsburgh Steelers hosting the Atlanta Falcons, showcasing a pair of fresh coaching regimes, most notably the Steelers breaking in a new head coach for the first time after 19 seasons under Mike Tomlin .

New head coach Mike McCarthy enjoyed a successful debut, guiding his squad to a 20-13 victory in his emotional reunion with Aaron Rodgers , a pairing that previously spent 13 seasons together in Green Bay and captured a Super Bowl title.

Playing in his 22nd and final NFL campaign as the oldest player in the league, the 42-year-old quarterback completed his evening throwing for 221 yards and a touchdown to tight end Pat Freiermuth in a steady, composed performance.

Despite securing the win, Rodgers proved true to his outspoken reputation during his post-game sideline interview with veteran Fox reporter Pam Oliver, sharply criticizing the officiating crew over several missed infractions. "I think we did a lot of good things out there," Rodgers stated.

"We had a chance to be really, really explosive. We had a couple drops, a couple off targets, a couple non-calls, looked like penalties." The legendary signal-caller specifically highlighted a glaring missed 40-yard pass interference penalty against Falcons star cornerback A.J. Terrell, noting it could easily have resulted in a touchdown.

Ultimately, it took a clutch defensive play from four-time All-Pro edge rusher T.J. Watt to secure the outcome, as Watt read a fourth-quarter screen pass intended for star running back Bijan Robinson and raced for an improbable pick-six.

The Steelers will now hit the road to face the New England Patriots before returning home to close out the month with a crucial divisional showdown against Cincinnati.

With the Baltimore Ravens looking electric after a 41-23 victory over the Indianapolis Colts and the Cincinnati Bengals ’ defense looking competent in a 33-27 victory against the Tampa Bay Buccaneers , the AFC North could once again go down to the wire.

articles.title: “The Steelers looked moribund”: Rodgers under pressure as Pittsburgh falls flat against Patriots
articles.standfirst: The loss highlighted a simple reality: the veteran cannot carry this offense by himself
articles.summary: The loss highlighted a simple reality: the veteran cannot carry this offense by himself
articles.body:
T he Pittsburgh Steelers entered the 2026 season believing they had assembled a roster capable of making noise in the AFC . Two games into the campaign, however, that optimism is already being tested. Sunday’s 20-3 loss to the New England Patriots was more than just a defeat. It was an offensive collapse that raised questions about whether Pittsburgh’s biggest offseason bets are going to pay off. The Steelers now sit at 1-1 and third place in the AFC North, but the bigger issue is how they looked getting there.

According to NFL.com senior news writer Kevin Patra, the Steelers appeared “moribund, out of sync and, frankly, boring” during the loss. It is difficult to argue with that assessment after watching an offense that struggled to sustain drives, failed to establish a running game and repeatedly put its quarterback in difficult situations.

The most glaring issue remains Aaron Rodgers

At 42 years old, Rodgers was brought in to stabilize the offense and elevate a team that believed it was only a quarterback away from contention. Instead, he endured a frustrating afternoon against New England. He struggled to navigate pressure, absorbed numerous hits and committed two costly fumbles that significantly altered the course of the game.

For a quarterback whose career has been defined by ball security and control, those mistakes stood out. The loss also highlighted a simple reality: Rodgers cannot carry this offense by himself. The Steelers invested heavily in DK Metcalf, expecting the star receiver to provide a dynamic complement in the passing game.

Through two weeks, that investment has yet to produce the expected results. Patra went so far as to call Metcalf a “net negative,” noting that the $32 million receiver has not played anywhere near the level Pittsburgh anticipated when it committed significant resources to acquiring him.

The issues extend beyond the passing game

Pittsburgh’s rushing attack has struggled to find traction, placing even more pressure on Rodgers and the receivers. Perhaps most surprising has been the performance of the offensive line. Entering the season, many analysts viewed the unit as one of the roster’s strengths. Against New England, however, it was overwhelmed. Pass protection broke down repeatedly, and the group failed to create consistent lanes in the running game.

When a veteran quarterback is constantly under pressure, the running game is ineffective and the receiving corps is not producing explosive plays, the result is exactly what Pittsburgh fans witnessed on Sunday: an offense that never seemed capable of taking control of the game. Still, before Steelers fans hit the panic button , some perspective is necessary.

The NFL season is only two weeks old. Teams routinely look dramatically different in September than they do in November and December. New offensive systems often take time to develop chemistry, particularly when a veteran quarterback is working with new teammates. Rodgers himself appeared to recognize that reality after the game.

“Can't feel sorry for ourselves. Can't point fingers. We've all got to play better,” Rodgers said. “The best teams are player-led teams, so we've got to keep taking the ownership.”

Rodgers taking accountability matters

Perhaps the most revealing part of his comments came when he acknowledged that communication between players and coaches must improve. “In a game like today where there wasn't a lot of flow to it, we need to be better, and it starts with me,” Rodgers added, emphasizing the importance of helping the coaching staff identify what is and is not working during games.

That accountability matters. One of the reasons Pittsburgh pursued Rodgers was his experience and leadership . If the offense is going to improve, it will likely start with the quarterback helping to diagnose and solve its issues. A 1-1 record is hardly cause for alarm, especially in September.

The AFC North remains tightly packed, and there is enough talent on the roster to expect better performances than what Pittsburgh showed in Foxborough. What Sunday's loss did reveal is that several key pieces of the offense have yet to click.

The offensive line has not played to expectations, the running game lacks rhythm, Metcalf has yet to emerge as a difference-maker and Rodgers has spent too much time operating under pressure. So is it time to panic? Not yet.

articles.title: Christian González shut down DK Metcalf and led the Patriots' defensive showcase against Pittsburgh
articles.standfirst: The Colombian directly covered the Steelers receiver on 34 plays and limited him to two receptions for eight yards on seven targets during New England's victory.
articles.summary: The Colombian directly covered the Steelers receiver on 34 plays and limited him to two receptions for eight yards on seven targets during New England's victory.
articles.body:
In Week 2 of the 2026 season, th e New England Patriots earned their first victory of the year by defeating the Pittsburgh Steelers 20-3, in a game marked by the dominance of their defense. Cornerback Christian González played a standout role by being tasked with directly covering DK Metcalf, one of Pittsburgh's top receivers.

González shadowed Metcalf on 34 plays , recording the highest total of his career while covering a single receiver in the same game. The Patriots coaching staff's strategy worked to perfection, taking away the main passing option in Pittsburgh's offense.

The result was a "shutout" for the history books

Metcalf was targeted nine times and finished with four receptions for 27 yards. When he was covered directly by González, he managed two receptions for eight yards on seven targets . The cornerback also recorded a pass defended, while New England's defense held Pittsburgh to three points.

During the game, Pittsburgh tried to create space by moving Metcalf around different areas of the field. Gonzalez, however, followed him even when the receiver lined up outside his usual position; however, th e Colombian cornerback's coverage completely shut down the Steelers' primary offensive strategy .

' Kevin Byard , Patriots safety, highlighted his teammate’s work after the game. "I don’t think (Metcalf) had a lot of fun at all," he said when asked about the matchup. Byard explained that, when González is lined up over the outside receiver, he trusts him to handle the coverage without needing any additional help.'

Cornerback's performance came just days after the Patriots secured his future with a four-year, $135 million contract extension, including $102 million guaranteed, a figure that positions him as the highest-paid player of South American roots in the history of the competition .

The Patriots held Pittsburgh to three points , sacked Rodgers four times and forced two turnovers. Elijah Ponder returned one of those recovered balls for a touchdown, while the defense preserved the result throughout the entire second half

After the victory, New England put behind them the 13-10 loss to Seattle in the opening game and moved to 1-1 . Their next matchup will be on Sunday, September 27 against the Jacksonville Jaguars at EverBank Stadium, in the third week of the regular season.

articles.title: “You never loved me!?” Mallory Edens just called out Aaron Rodgers in the wildest way possible
articles.standfirst: Rodgers and Edens are believed to have dated between 2022 and 2024.
articles.summary: Rodgers and Edens are believed to have dated between 2022 and 2024.
articles.body:
A aron Rodgers ’ former girlfriend Mallory Edens has turned the Pittsburgh Steelers ’ latest relationship confession into an unexpected promotional opportunity for her new romantic drama. Mallory , the daughter of Milwaukee Bucks owner Wes Edens , and Rodgers were first linked in 2022, though neither publicly defined the relationship in detail – but the relationship didn’t seem to last long.

By December 2024, Rodgers was calling Brittani his girlfriend and has since gone on to marry her, although information about the couple and their relationship are few and far between. Now promoting Charlie Harper , Edens addressed her former relationship without naming Rodgers via Instagram, turning his relationship comments into a cheeky pitch for her own romantic drama. The post came after Rodgers appeared on Cam Heyward 's Not Just Football podcast and discussed Brittani , saying they first met in 2017 and that he knew she was the one despite dating other women across the period before they began dating. "My ex is currently on a press tour talking about how he never loved anyone he dated after 2017,” Edens wrote. “Unfortunately for him, I am also on a press tour, for a movie inspired by how down bad I was. Really exciting time for competing narratives!!" Charlie Harper follows a couple whose romance begins to fracture as their lives move in different directions. Edens produced the film, which is scheduled to arrive in theaters Friday.

Rob Gronkowski believes Aaron Rodgers thinks he should have retired

Rodgers ' relationship revelations are unfolding alongside a difficult start to his 22nd NFL season as Pittsburgh suffered a Week 2 loss to the New England Patriots to leave the side 1-1. The Patriots beat the Steelers 20-3 on a day in which Mike McCarthy ’s offense simply did not click and New England did not need a high score to go on to secure victory after their defeat to the Seattle Seahawks . Through two games, he has completed 59.5% of his passes with one touchdown and one interception, whilst he has also taken six sacks and fumbled twice as Pittsburgh searches for answers. And now Rob Gronkowski believes the veteran quarterback may regret returning to the sport after retirement was reportedly under consideration following the dismal start to the year. “Aaron Rodgers is probably thinking that he should have retired last year,” Gronkowski said. “After watching the first two weeks, I’m saying that’s what he was probably thinking.” There is still time for Rodgers and the Steelers to change the narrative, particularly with a new playcaller and new offensive additions such as Michael Pittman Jr. and Rico Dowdle . But the next two weeks bring Pittsburgh 's first two divisional games against the Cincinnati Bengals and Cleveland Browns , so a response must come quickly if the team aims to avoid being left behind in the AFC North .

articles.title: Blood is thicker than water: Jordan Rodgers fiercely defends brother Aaron after years of silence
articles.standfirst: The younger Rodgers urged patience with Pittsburgh
articles.summary: The younger Rodgers urged patience with Pittsburgh
articles.body:
Jordan Rodgers spent years publicly separated from one of the most recognizable quarterbacks in NFL history. Now, only weeks after he and Aaron Rodgers quietly reconnected, he is defending his older brother on national television.

Appearing on ESPN’s First Take, Jordan pushed back against the early criticism surrounding Aaron ’s first two games of the 2026 season with the Pittsburgh Steelers . His argument was that the offense has been closer to clicking than the box scores indicate.

“I think if you truly watched Week 1, this was a team that was a few drops and a few missed calls away from being absolutely explosive, like we haven’t seen out of the Steelers in a really long time,” Jordan said.

“Rodgers was actually very accurate down the field,” Jordan added. “The throws that were not completed because of either a non-call or a drop down the field were on the money. Not trying to be a homer.”

That last remark drew laughs from the panel, but it also underscored how dramatically the brothers’ relationship has changed.

Jordan’s tone a striking departure from the past

Their estrangement became public in 2016, when Jordan discussed the family divide while appearing on The Bachelorette.

“Me and Aaron don’t really have that much of a relationship,” Jordan said at the time. “It’s just kind of the way he’s chosen to do life and I’ve chosen to stay close with my family and my parents and my brother.”

That distance lasted for years. Aaron revealed earlier this month on Cam Heyward’s Not Just Football podcast that the brothers had recently spoken again.

“I went out to Nashville and met with my older brother,” Aaron said. “A couple weeks after that, I met with my little brother. It was cool.”

He described the meeting with Jordan as a “tough conversation” and credited his wife, Brittani, with helping him reach a better place mentally.

“I’m in a much better headspace,” Aaron went on. “My wife deserves a lot of the credit for that just to be even able to get to that point where I could think about having the conversation.”

Pittsburgh reunion with Mike McCarthy also needs time

Jordan also discussed Aaron ’s second chapter with Mike McCarthy , who coached him for more than a decade in Green Bay before their relationship deteriorated.

“The other aspect that I think is still a feeling out process, Rodgers and McCarthy are like that ex you ended up getting back together with after a long time,” Jordan said.

“You’re like, ‘Things are better. We’re different people. We’re still trying to figure out those quirks we had when we were in a relationship.’ I think that’s going to take time.”

Pittsburgh is 1-1 entering Week 3, with Aaron completing 59.5% of his passes for 408 yards, one touchdown and one interception. Jordan’s broader message was patience.

After years when almost every public mention of the Rodgers brothers centered on their estrangement, Wednesday offered something much more ordinary, in one brother breaking down the other’s quarterback play and, almost accidentally, admitting he was rooting for him.

articles.title: Steelers have their own version of Daejon Love: Pittsburgh rookie impersonated by scammer
articles.standfirst: The San Francisco 49ers-Daejon Love scam has opened up a can of worms apparently.
articles.summary: The San Francisco 49ers-Daejon Love scam has opened up a can of worms apparently.
articles.body:
One of the craziest storylines of the 2026 NFL season actually had nothing to do with a real NFL player. The San Francisco 49ers franchise was flung into the limelight, very unwantedly, when news surfaced of a scammer pretending to be one of their players.

Daejon Love was the culprit, using 49ers gear and a fake social media account to dupe women into sending him money for fraudulent investments. Alongside posing as a real estate developer, Love ended up swindling victims out of a total of $1.3 million . He has since been arrested.

Eli Heidenreich impersonator scams two local women out of $1,000

As it turns out, other scammers have been galvanized by Love's actions . A report recently surfaced that a different scammer posed as Pittsburgh Steelers rookie running back Eli Heidenreich and was able to muster $1,000 from two women , according to the Pennsylvania State Police .

Unfortunately, no suspects have been identified as of yet . It's unclear if there were more victims. This is a different type of scam since the culprit is actually posing as a real NFL player. Love simply created a false persona.

This is quite the welcome to the city of Pittsburgh for the rookie. Heidenreich was selected in the seventh round of the 2026 NFL Draft by the Steelers in April. He went to school at Navy , so he surely won't find the situation funny in any way.
